holidays.name: National Rubber Ducky Day
holidays.description: Grab your favorite yellow bath buddy and give it a place of honor. Today is for squeaky, floating, bathtub-dwelling joy. Run a bubble bath, line up a flotilla of ducks, or just give your desk duck a little squeeze.
holidays.origin: The rubber duck took off with the rise of the rubber industry in the late 1800s. Its pop culture fame got a boost in 1970, when Ernie sang "Rubber Duckie" on Sesame Street. The day is an unofficial observance tied to that beloved bath toy.
holidays.funFact: Sculptor Peter Ganine is credited with popularizing the rubber duck, and the toy has since become one of the most recognizable bath-time icons in the world.

holidays.name: National Sticker Day
holidays.description: Peel, stick, and decorate everything in sight. Laptops, water bottles, notebooks, and fridge doors are all fair game. Dig out your old sticker collection and give it some well-deserved attention.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the humble adhesive sticker and the way it lets us express ourselves anywhere.
holidays.funFact: Stickers have been a classic reward for kids for generations, and they are also a favorite way for adults to personalize their gear.

holidays.name: National Peach Melba Day
holidays.description: Today is a good day for a fancy dessert. Peach Melba pairs poached peaches with vanilla ice cream and raspberry sauce. It is simple, elegant, and tastes like a night at the opera.
holidays.origin: The dessert was created by French chef Auguste Escoffier in honor of Australian opera singer Nellie Melba. The day is an unofficial observance celebrating the classic treat.
holidays.funFact: Nellie Melba also inspired Melba toast, another dish named in her honor.
